asyncapi.title: /stt/turns/websocket
asyncapi.description:
Realtime speech transcription with built-in turn detection

<Note>
`ink-2` supports English, French, Hindi, Japanese, and Spanish. `ink-preview` supports [44 languages](/use-the-api/stt/languages).
Both detect the language automatically.
</Note>

model.description:
ID of the model to use for transcription: `ink-2` or `ink-preview`.

See [Models](/build-with-cartesia/stt/latest) for details.

encoding.description:
The encoding of the raw audio you send. The server uses it to read your audio.

For help choosing an encoding, see [Audio Input](/build-with-cartesia/stt/audio-input).

sample_rate.description: The sample rate of the audio in Hz, from 8000 to 48000

language_hint.description:
Used by `ink-preview` only. `ink-2` returns an error.

A language to steer transcription toward. Hints don't stop the model from transcribing other languages.

To pass several, repeat the `language_hint` query parameter. You can pass up to 6. Use base codes from [Languages](/use-the-api/stt/languages), such as `pt`, not `pt-BR`. `language_hints` is also accepted as an alias.

Example: `?language_hint=hi&language_hint=en`

See [Languages](/use-the-api/stt/languages#language-hints) for details.

turn_start_threshold.description:
Threshold above which the turn starts. Default: 0.8. Range: 0.5–0.9. Must stay above `turn_eager_end_threshold`.

See [Configuring turn detection](/use-the-api/stt/turns#configuring-turn-detection) for details.

turn_eager_end_threshold.description:
Threshold below which `turn.eager_end` fires. Default: 0.6. Range: 0.3–0.8. Must stay between `turn_end_threshold` and `turn_start_threshold`.

See [Configuring turn detection](/use-the-api/stt/turns#configuring-turn-detection) for details.

turn_end_threshold.description:
Threshold below which the turn ends. Default: 0.3. Range: 0.05–0.5. Must stay below `turn_eager_end_threshold`.

See [Configuring turn detection](/use-the-api/stt/turns#configuring-turn-detection) for details.

turn_end_timeout_ms.description:
The longest the model waits after the user stops speaking before it ends the turn, in milliseconds. Default: 5600. Range: 640–11200.

See [Configuring turn detection](/use-the-api/stt/turns#configuring-turn-detection) for details.

keyterm.description:
Key terms that help the model recognize specific words and phrases.

To pass several, repeat the `keyterm` query parameter. `ink-preview` accepts up to 500 keyterms totaling 5,000 characters. `ink-2` accepts up to 100 totaling 1,200. To boost one multi-word phrase, join the words with `%20`. `keyterms` is accepted as an alias.

URLs longer than about 8 KB are rejected with HTTP 414. With `ink-preview`, send long lists in a `config` message after you connect.

Example: `?keyterm=Ink%202&keyterm=Cartesia`

See [Keyterm prompting](/use-the-api/stt/keyterms) for details.

asyncapi.title: /stt/websocket
asyncapi.description:
Realtime speech transcription without turn detection

<Note>
  Send the `finalize` command to trigger transcription. See [Compare STT Endpoints](/use-the-api/stt/compare-endpoints) for details.
</Note>

model.description:
ID of the model to use for transcription.

See [Models](/build-with-cartesia/stt/latest) for details.

encoding.description:
The encoding of the raw audio you send. The server uses it to read your audio.

For help choosing an encoding, see [Audio Input](/build-with-cartesia/stt/audio-input).

sample_rate.description: The sample rate of the audio in Hz, from 8000 to 48000

language_hint.description:
Used by `ink-preview` only. `ink-2` returns an error.

A language to steer transcription toward. Hints don't stop the model from transcribing other languages.

To pass several, repeat the `language_hint` query parameter. You can pass up to 6. Use base codes from [Languages](/use-the-api/stt/languages), such as `pt`, not `pt-BR`. `language_hints` is also accepted as an alias.

Example: `?language_hint=hi&language_hint=en`

See [Languages](/use-the-api/stt/languages#language-hints) for details.

language.description:
Used by `ink-whisper` models only. Leave it out with `ink-2` and `ink-preview`, which detect the language automatically. To steer `ink-preview` toward a language, use `language_hint`.

With `ink-whisper`, set this to the language code of the audio. If you leave it out, it defaults to `en`, and speech in other languages can come back translated into English.

See [Older models](/build-with-cartesia/stt/older-models#ink-whisper) for all options.

min_volume.description:
Used by `ink-whisper` models only.

Sets what counts as silence when the API finalizes transcripts automatically. Range: 0.0–1.0.

Lower values pick up quiet audio.
Higher values filter noisy audio more.

max_silence_duration_secs.description:
Used by `ink-whisper` models only.

The longest silence, in seconds, before the API finalizes the transcript automatically.

Lower values finalize transcripts sooner.
Higher values allow longer pauses within an utterance.

keyterm.description:
Used by `ink-2` and `ink-preview` only.

Key terms that help the model recognize specific words and phrases.

To pass several, repeat the `keyterm` query parameter. `ink-preview` accepts up to 500 keyterms totaling 5,000 characters. `ink-2` accepts up to 100 totaling 1,200. To boost one multi-word phrase, join the words with `%20`. `keyterms` is accepted as an alias.

URLs longer than about 8 KB are rejected with HTTP 414. With `ink-preview`, send long lists in a `config` message after you connect.

Example: `?keyterm=Ink%202&keyterm=Cartesia`

See [Keyterm prompting](/use-the-api/stt/keyterms) for details.

properties.name: model_id

properties.name: transcript

properties.name: voice
properties.description: The voice to use for generation. Pass either a voice ID string or an object with a required `id` (additional object fields may be added in future API versions). Use the same value for all generation requests made to the same context. Embeddings are not accepted in this API version.

properties.name: language
properties.description: The transcript's language or locale. Use a base language code such as `en` or a regional locale code such as `en-GB`. `language` and `locale` accept the same values. Set one or the other, never both; setting both returns an error. The enum lists canonical codes; matching is case-insensitive, and underscore locale aliases such as `en_GB` are also accepted. See [supported codes](/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/advanced-capabilities#which-locales-are-supported).

properties.name: locale

See [supported codes](/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/advanced-capabilities#which-locales-are-supported).

properties.name: accent
properties.description: Usually unnecessary: Cartesia picks the closest accent the voice supports for the requested `language` or `locale`. Set it only to make a [multilingual voice](/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/multilingual-voices) sound accented (e.g. speak English with a French accent). Must come from the voice's [Get Voice `accents` field](/api-reference/voices/get#response-accents). Learn more [here](/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/multilingual-voices#using-a-multilingual-voice).

properties.name: normalization
properties.description: Text normalization. `auto` (initial default) runs the locale-aware normalizer, `off` skips it, or pass a language or locale code (for example `en` or `en-IN`) to pin the normalizer independently of the generation language. If omitted on a later request in the same context, the previous value is reused. See [Text Normalization](/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/text-normalization).

properties.name: continue
properties.description:

  - Set to `false` on the last `transcript` chunk for this context to minimize latency
